back: Ratio of the equilibrium concentrations of a solute in two immiscible solvents, at a given temperature, same molecular state in both.
m₁ = m₀ × V_aq/(V_aq + Kpc × V_org), with Kpc = [organic]/[aqueous].
Several small portions of solvent extract more than one large portion of the same total volume.
Non-polar solutes have large Kpc(organic/water); ionic or hydrogen-bonding solutes have small values.
Kpc fails if the solute dissociates (e.g. in water) or dimerises (e.g. ethanoic acid in non-polar solvents).
Hexane and ether float on water; dichloromethane and trichloromethane sink.
Solutes are shared between a stationary and a mobile phase; larger Kpc(mobile/stationary) means further travel.
Shake, vent through the tap, let layers separate, run off the lower layer; repeat with fresh solvent.
